statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 18% while Stress remains elevated at 58%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the watch threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON. The elevated Stress reading reflects a long-end Treasury selloff and elevated oil rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 price path. The 12:30-14:30 UTC macro block is marked as the session's narrow danger window.
headline: Low Tail with elevated Stress as a bond selloff meets an orderly Nasdaq-100 recovery
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,478.86 on Sep 24, up 0.03%, after trading down to 30,204.16 intraday and recovering into the close as reported hopes of a phased US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz offset a deepening global bond selloff. That intraday reversal is the key evidence for the current assessment: retracements are working, which argues against the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures. Overnight NQ futures near 30,802 have held a narrow 30,679-30,814 band, and the VIX at 15.67 leaves implied volatility benign. The stress side of the picture is genuine. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.16% at roughly a 19-year high, the 30-year near 5.4% at its highest since 2004, and markets have begun pricing rate hikes rather than cuts. Oil remains elevated with WTI near $92.89 and Brent near or above $100 despite a de-escalation-driven pullback. Latest-session breadth is dispersed rather than aligned, with META up 4.5% and Alphabet up 1.3% against ARM down 7.9% and Qualcomm down 1.5%, a pattern that widens ranges rather than producing index-level one-way structure. Tail is therefore held at 18 while Stress is carried at 58.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours Claude Tail readings ranged from 17 to 25 while Stress held between 50 and 59. Tail peaked at 25 in the 09:00 UTC European-morning slot, the only orange reading of the window, then eased through the US session as the Nasdaq-100 recovered from its intraday low. The overnight hours since the US close have been consistently green with Tail between 17 and 18, reflecting an orderly, two-sided futures path against a persistently elevated Stress backdrop.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to stay in the low-to-watch range across the coming session. It steps into the WATCH band from the 07:00 UTC European cash open, peaks at 24 across the 13:00-14:00 UTC window covering the US cash open, the 12:30 UTC Durable Goods release and the 14:00 UTC Michigan sentiment final, then decays through the US afternoon if post-release price discovery stays orderly. From the 21:00 UTC CME weekend halt no continuous NQ price discovery exists, so Tail falls to 15 and Confidence eases toward 81 to reflect the absence of live price-path evidence. Weekend Hormuz headline risk transfers to the Sunday reopen, outside this window.
